text.p: Indian police said on Monday that they had failed to track down former "Bandit Queen" Phoolan Devi, a low-caste member of parliament wanted in several dozen criminal cases including murder.
"We have not been able to arrest her, despite our best efforts," H.D. Rao, police chief in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, told reporters in the state capital Lucknow.
"Police parties have been trying to track her down, but she is not to be found."

Devi, who belongs to the low-caste Mallah community of boatmen, shot to notoriety after 22 upper-caste men were killed in a massacre at Behmai village, near the industrial town of Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh in 1981.
She was accused of leading a gang in the massacre but denied the charges. Devi surrendered to the police in 1983 under a special amnesty offered by the central state of Madhya Pradesh.

Devi spent more than 10 years in prison before being released in 1994. Movie maker Sekhar Kapoor portrayed Devi as a low-caste heroine in the biographical film "Bandit Queen" which won praise at several international film festivals.
A Kanpur judge recently issued warrants for her re-arrest to face trial in 57 pending cases, including murder.

Last week, the Supreme Court rejected Devi's plea to have all her cases transferred to a Delhi court. Her lawyers told the Supreme Court that Devi, now a member of parliament, would surrender on Tuesday before a judge in Kanpur.
But her counsel Nand Lal Jaiswal said on Monday that Devi was under no obligation to appear in court.

"Phoolan Devi neither made any such assurance nor is she obliged to do so," he said, adding that he had gone to the high court in Allahabad town, challenging the jurisdiction of a law under which she has been sought.
United News of India said police trying to serve an arrest warrant had searched Devi's house in New Delhi to no avail.
